h1: Grain and Wheat Warehouses in Pakistan: Dry, Ventilated Steel Storage
quickAnswer: Grain must stay dry and cool. A steel grain warehouse needs a tight roof, steady ventilation and walls strong enough to hold the sideways push of the grain.
alt: Pile of wheat inside a ventilated steel grain warehouse.

faq.q: How do you keep grain dry?
faq.a: Through a tight roof, a sealed floor and steady ventilation.

faq.q: Do you make bins and hoppers?
faq.a: Yes. See the Hoppers and Bins page.

blocks.text: Grain must stay dry and cool. Moisture causes mold, insects and heat inside the pile. The building needs a tight roof, good ventilation and strong walls that can hold the sideways push of grain.

Stored grain pushes on the walls, so the wall frames and bracing are designed for this load. Ridge vents and louvers keep air moving above the grain. A leak-free roof with good sheet laps and trims keeps the wheat dry. A raised, sealed floor limits moisture from the ground. Wide doors and driveways allow trucks and loaders to enter. Grain dust and moisture can attack steel, so a good coating extends the life of the frame. See Painting.
A steel grain warehouse is quick to build, which matters before the harvest and procurement seasons. Large clear spans give you the volume you need without inner columns.
